_readme: FIAT ART PASS (15 Oct, Matt; status.md item 19): the Gamekeeper's two uniques to art/items/ (the game picks them up by name), and the pistol's, the SMG's and the nail gun's hands redrawn down the sight to art/fight_new/.
Look at art/fight_new/ first; copy the ones that read over art/fight/hands_<kind>.png (or say, and Claude will). The muzzle flash's points (RunView.MUZZLE) are read off them again after.

Run: godot --headless --script res://tools/pixellab_batch_v2.gd ++ --manifest res://tools/pixellab_art_pass_manifest.json   (++ --dry-run to list; one that came out wrong: ++ --only <name> ++ --force).

jobs.description: A realistic painted pixel-art still-life of a single gamekeeper's twelve-bore pump-action shotgun, seen exactly side-on with the muzzle pointing left, laid level and filling the frame left to right: a walnut stock oiled dark by forty years of hands, a cracked leather sling, the blueing worn silver at the pump, three brass-capped cartridges held to the stock by a band of inner tube. One object centred and filling the frame, soft directional overcast daylight, natural material rendering with fine detail and painterly shading; no black outlines, no flat cel shading, not anime, not a cartoon, not a glossy video-game item; the look of a real object photographed on a grey day in a country that has run out of money. Muted cool northern palette, worn and repaired, nothing new. Nothing else in the frame, no hands, no person, no text, no logos, a plain dark neutral background.
jobs._where: unique: The Keeper's Twelve-Bore (the Gamekeeper's, B8.1; on the Pump shotgun's picture till now)

jobs.description: A realistic painted pixel-art still-life of a single gamekeeper's waxed cotton field jacket, hung flat as if on a hook, seen from the front, filling the frame top to bottom: olive gone nearly black with rewaxing, a brown corduroy collar worn shiny, big bellows pockets sagging with cartridges, a tear at the elbow stitched shut with fishing line, a game pocket at the back bulging. One object centred and filling the frame, soft directional overcast daylight, natural material rendering with fine detail and painterly shading; no black outlines, no flat cel shading, not anime, not a cartoon, not a glossy video-game item; the look of a real object photographed on a grey day in a country that has run out of money. Muted cool northern palette, worn and repaired, nothing new. Nothing else in the frame, no hands, no person, no text, no logos, a plain dark neutral background.
jobs._where: unique: The Keeper's Wax Jacket (the Gamekeeper's, B8.1; on the Padded jacket's picture till now)

jobs.description: First-person view of the player's own two hands in fingerless wool gloves holding an old revolver in a two-handed grip, arms out, seen from behind and just above as the player aims it, the muzzle pointing straight away from the viewer up and into the frame toward its centre, the gun foreshortened along its length like a rifle shouldered in a first-person game - not side-on, not across the frame, the front sight and the top of the cylinder showing, one thumb over the other, coming in from the bottom right corner of the frame, as in a light-gun arcade game; the sleeves of a worn work jacket at the wrists. Only the hands and what they hold, coming in from the bottom right edge. Realistic painted pixel art, soft overcast light, muted cool northern palette, worn and lived-in, post-collapse Britain on a grey day; no black outlines, not anime, not a cartoon, not glossy; no text, no logos.
jobs._where: your hands: pistol, down the sight (was side-on)
